title: Transmission cooler locations and fluid routes
introduction:
Choose the drawing under the heading for the car’s engine, then match its callouts to the table directly below it. The figures locate the cooler and hose assembly, the fitting latches, and the paired tubes running between the cooler and transmission.

I follow the arrows as separate outward and return lanes. In these drawings, red arrows follow the orange cooler inlet tube from the transmission toward the cooler; turquoise arrows follow the green outlet tube back toward the transmission. “Inlet” and “outlet” are named from the cooler’s point of view—handy to remember when the plumbing starts looking like a bowl of spaghetti.

Use the drawings to recognize the route and connections. They do not provide in-car access, latch-release movements, disconnection instructions, fluid specifications or a cooling-system test.

edits.why: The cooler is at the left of this view and the transmission at the right. The fitting latches are at the hose-to-tube connections near the cooler. Follow the paired tubes past the visible supports to their transmission connections; use this engine’s drawing to recognize their bends and bracket locations.

This view shows the paired tubes passing through a shared support beneath the bellhousing and another support farther toward the cooler. I use the bends and supports to orient the route, then the adjacent table to identify each callout.

This layout shows additional changes in tube direction and a shaped support beneath the bellhousing. Trace each colored tube continuously between the cooler-side connections and transmission so a nearby bracket or crossing does not send you along the wrong route.
